Meet DecepticonX

DecepticonX — we love technology, AI, and turning ideas into products. For NASA Space Apps, we are exploring “Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map”, combining AI, NASA data, maps, and UI/UX.

What we bring:

AI/ML and full-stack development

GIS, maps, and data analysis

UI/UX, research, and prototyping

Why join ?
We want teammates who love to build, learn, and contribute. We welcome skills in space science, GIS, AI/ML, 3D, and design.

Ideas Beyond Boundaries.

MARS-X is an interactive Mars exploration and terrain-intelligence platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It transforms authentic planetary datasets into a unified environment for exploring Martian landscapes, discovering scientifically significant locations, analysing terrain, and planning terrain-aware Marswalk routes.

The platform integrates multi-resolution elevation models, orbital imagery, geological maps, thermal inertia data, rover observations, and atmospheric climatology. Its capabilities include interactive planetary mapping, AI-assisted scientific discovery, terrain slope analysis, A* route optimisation, multi-stop science traverses, elevation profiling, and environmental intelligence.

By connecting scientific evidence with geospatial analysis and route planning, MARS-X makes complex Mars data more accessible and useful for understanding potential exploration locations. It promotes evidence-based planetary exploration while clearly distinguishing observations, derived measurements, models, and scientific hypotheses.

MARS-X aims to bridge the gap between planetary science datasets and practical exploration planning, providing a foundation for future research into Martian surface exploration.
details:
MARS-X — Planetary Terrain Intelligence & Marswalk Navigation

MARS-X is an interactive planetary exploration and terrain-intelligence platform designed to support the planning and analysis of surface exploration on Mars. It transforms authentic Martian scientific datasets into an integrated environment where users can explore the planet, investigate geological features, analyse terrain, and plan terrain-aware Marswalk routes.

The platform combines multi-resolution elevation datasets, geological maps, orbital imagery, thermal inertia products, rover meteorological observations, and atmospheric climatology. Its interactive exploration console displays Mars terrain and scientific layers, while the Science Discovery system identifies candidate locations of geological and scientific interest and presents the evidence behind each discovery.

MARS-X includes a terrain intelligence engine that calculates slope and evaluates terrain at different spatial resolutions. Its Marswalk planner uses A* pathfinding and Dijkstra-based comparisons to generate routes using elevation and terrain-derived analytical costs. Multi-stop science traverses allow users to plan routes connecting multiple investigation locations. Route Intelligence further evaluates elevation profiles, slope exposure, roughness, geological context, and thermal inertia.

The Environmental Intelligence module combines analytical atmospheric approximations, deterministic solar geometry, historical MEDA and REMS rover observations, and Mars Climate Database climatology. It distinguishes modelled estimates, historical observations, derived measurements, and scientific interpretations rather than presenting them as live weather forecasts.

The project was developed using Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, MapLibre GL JS, Python, FastAPI, Pydantic, NumPy, Rasterio, GeoPandas, Shapely, and GDAL. Data processing uses planetary geospatial formats and coordinate-reference systems, including PDS products, GeoTIFF, GeoJSON, and Mars-specific CRS definitions.

MARS-X is creative because it brings planetary datasets that are normally explored through separate scientific tools into one connected exploration workflow. Instead of treating a Mars map as a visualisation alone, it connects scientific evidence, terrain analysis, geological discovery, environmental context, and route optimisation.

The intended impact is to make authentic Mars science more accessible, encourage evidence-based planetary exploration, and demonstrate how scientific datasets and geospatial algorithms can support future surface-mission research. The system is an experimental research and planning platform, not a certified astronaut-safety system or operational mission-control tool.

During development, the team prioritised scientific provenance, coordinate-reference-system consistency, resolution awareness, reproducibility, transparent uncertainty, data integrity, and clear distinctions between observations, derived measurements, models, and hypotheses.
